## MEASURED STATE — read this first, and do not re-derive it

This node was written before any of the work it adopts had landed. Everything below was
measured on this host today; where it disagrees with the older prose further down, this
section wins. Where it disagrees with **your own measurement**, your measurement wins and
you should say so.

### What is pinned here right now, on ai-orchestrator origin/main

    config/onepipeline.version     0.10.1
    config/oneagentgraph.version   0.3.6
    config/onevcs.version          0.10.0
    config/oneharness.version      0.10.2
    config/onejudge.version        0.4.0
    config/onepipeline-ui.version  0.6.2

### What is actually in force, measured from the installed binary

    strings -a "$(readlink -f "$(command -v onepipeline)")" \
      | grep -oE '(onevcs|oneagentgraph|onejudge)-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | sort -u

reports `oneagentgraph-0.3.6`, `onejudge-0.5.0`, `onevcs-0.10.0`.

**So the gate concept is still in force on this host.** onevcs 0.10.0 is a release that
still has it. That is precisely the state PART 2 exists to change, and it is why PART 1's
lockfile evidence is the hinge of this whole node rather than paperwork.

### What has shipped upstream

  - onevcs **v0.11.0** — the gate concept removed entirely (PR #65). Released.
  - onevcs PR #63 — publication evidence and await-merge. Merged.
  - oneagentgraph **0.3.5** — the engineer role bar corrected (PR #69). Released;
    0.3.6 is newer still and is what is pinned and in force.
  - onepipeline **v0.10.0** — publication failure routing (PR #93). Released.
  - onepipeline **v0.10.1** — resolves oneagentgraph 0.3.6. Released and adopted here.

### What this node waits on — measured after the task was first written

**It has shipped.** onepipeline's relink onto onevcs 0.11.0 was PR #98; it merged at
`2026-08-22T16:04:36Z` as `35c63b92`, and **v0.11.0 was tagged at `16:51:59Z`**. Confirm both
yourself rather than taking them from here.

What was still true at `16:52Z` and is the one thing you may have to wait on: **PyPI carried
`onepipeline-cli` 0.10.1, not 0.11.0** — the `Release` workflow was still building the wheel.
Check before you install:

    curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/onepipeline-cli/json | python3 -c "import sys,json;print('0.11.0' in json.load(sys.stdin)['releases'])"

If that answers `False`, **wait for it rather than working around it.** Do not build from source,
do not install from a git ref, and do not pin a version the registry does not carry — session
setup installs the pinned wheel from PyPI and a pin it cannot resolve breaks this host for every
other run on it. Poll on a sensible interval and say in your report how long you waited.

Once it is there: pin it, install it, and prove it with the `strings` command above plus the
wheel's CycloneDX SBOM the way `tests/test_linked_libraries.py` does. **If the installed binary
does not report `onevcs-0.11.0`, stop and say so** rather than recording an adoption that did not
happen — that check is the whole point of this node and a green pin over a binary that links
something else is exactly the failure this repository has been burned by twice.

### The prose edits are mechanically gated — find them from the gate, not by reading around

`tests/test_linked_libraries.py` carries `LINKED_VERSION_CLAIMS`: a map of crate → file →
the exact sentence that file must spell for the **measured** linked version. It reads the
`onepipeline-cli` wheel's CycloneDX SBOM and fails when a sentence names a different release
from the one that wheel actually linked. So the moment you move
`config/onepipeline.version`, that gate tells you precisely which sentences in which files
are now false.

At the time this task was written it holds `onevcs` claims in `AGENTS.md`,
`docs/repo-lifecycle.md` (two sentences), and `docs/onejudge-integration.md`, and
`oneagentgraph` claims in `personas/README.md`, `docs/dag-ui.md`, and
`docs/onejudge-integration.md`. Read the map itself rather than trusting that list — it is
the source and this paragraph is a copy.
